newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond market to load up on new supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond market to load up on new supply.

text.p: Corporate bond issuers are expected to bring a load of new supply to market ahead of Friday's U.S. employment report and next week's U.S. Presidential elections, dealers said.
"Issuers will have a small window to get some paper done today and tomorrow before Friday's employment data and next week's elections," one syndicate source said.
"There's still money there but investors are still pretty picky...they're better buyers on dips," he added.
A few investment grade issues and lots of high-yield debt junk supply are expected to come to market.
"Deals are getting done very successfully even though spreads are tight...and issuers are taking advantage of that," said another syndicate source.
Issuers are expected to meet their financing needs near-term as upcoming market holidays and the end of the calendar year make for difficult structuring of new deals as desks become thinly staffed.
"Given the good rate environment this is a good opportunity for issuers to put their last financing of the year on the books," the syndicate source added.
So far two investment grade issuers have tapped the market on Tuesday, dealers said.

GTE-North priced $250 million in 12-year A1/AA rated debentures via competitive bid. The deal, which was won by Morgan Stanley, priced to yield 47 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, syndicate sources said.
Also, Pohang Iron and Steel priced $300 million in A2/A-plus rated 10-year notes to yield 70 basis points over Treasuries via lead manager Salomon Brothers.
Meanwhile, Hongkong Shanghai Bank-America is also expected to issue $300 million in Baa1/A-minus rated 10-year debt.
The calendar for yankee debt issuance is also expected to pick up significantly over the next week, dealers added.
"We should see more issues in the next five to seven business days with the lion's share of it from issuers outside of the United States," a syndicate source said.
Korea Development Bank is expected to lead the way with $500 million in 10-year global debt, dealers said.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is up 46/32 at 100-10/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
